A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deep Augmentation study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original sentence-embedding, image, and graph experiments, together with supervised comparisons and extensive appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds statistical summaries and supervised representation diagnostics.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains layer-targeted dropout or PCA, optional stop-gradient, augmentation of 50% of each batch, and the same network decomposition. CKA-guided layer selection is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Wikipedia/STS, CIFAR10/100, ImageNet100, and four graph datasets. Supervised learning, MLM-only learning, and bidirectional CIFAR transfer already appear in v2; v3's diagnostics concern retained coverage.

E2.justification: The representation-analysis comparisons add regular supervised counterparts and a randomly initialized sentence-model reference (Table 8 and Figures 54, 57–58). The main benchmark comparator sets remain SimCSE, SimCLR, and GCL.

E3.justification: v3 extends supervised-model evaluation to CKA and alignment/uniformity, using validation-label sentence comparisons and fixed SimCLR image augmentations (Appendices D–E). The previously stated training budgets, architectures, and dataset splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands mechanism testing through supervised-versus-contrastive CKA comparisons, supervised alignment/uniformity analyses, and failed-model and random-initialization diagnostics (Appendices D–E). Appendix A.2 also adds a dropped-node-proportion analysis. These additions directly investigate the contrasting supervised and self-supervised behavior.

E5.justification: v3 adds STS ± statistics in Table 2, error bars in Figure 2, and explicitly described supervised CIFAR standard deviations in Figure 21. Graph standard deviations already existed. Run counts remain unspecified, as do the statistical meanings of the STS ± values and Figure 2 error bars.

E6.justification: Original headline benchmark scores are retained. v3 adds STS summaries in Table 2 (averages 75.61±0.924 for SimCSE and 76.56±0.161 for DeepAug), revises Figure 2's central curves, and adds supervised representation results in Table 8 and Figures 52, 54, 57–58. These are additional or revised results, not established version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix E adds an explicit data-processing-inequality argument, I(X;Y) ≥ I(X;f(Y)), connecting deterministic transformations with information removal. The existing method equations and PCA definition remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The performance and layer-selection contributions remain. The abstract, contribution bullets, and discussion narrow the collapse framing toward co-adaptation and spurious alignment, and withdraw the suggestion that collapse benefits supervised learning.

C2.justification: v2 suggests supervised degradation may reflect removal of beneficial collapse. v3 instead argues that labels already counteract spurious alignment and reduce co-adaptation. It adds the qualification that extremely low co-adaptation can accompany failure, and explains limitations of alignment/uniformity comparisons and their relationship to downstream performance.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, training budgets, batch size, augmentation code, layer-placement descriptions, and code-link targets are retained. The new dropped-node table calculates proportions from previously supplied layer counts rather than disclosing a different implementation.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained. Section 6 weakens the direct analogy with Chen and He's collapse prevention, while Section 6.2 and Appendix D explicitly distinguish SimCSE-style class-based alignment from Wang and Isola's augmentation-based formulation.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on the abstract, contribution bullets, analysis, and discussion. Appendix A.2/A.3 are reordered, a separate alignment/uniformity appendix is inserted, and the generic Impact Statement is removed. Most existing prose and section organization remain.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to predominantly single-column presentation, with different typography and extensively resized and relocated figures. v3 adds three tables and five figure displays, redraws Figure 2 with error bars, and introduces supervised comparison panels while retaining earlier figures.

improvement.justification: The new supervised diagnostics and failure example support a more qualified interpretation of co-adaptation, while expanded uncertainty reporting improves empirical transparency. These are useful gains without changing the method or original benchmark conclusions. Their benefit is limited by unspecified run counts and the unexplained coexistence of the original STS table and the new ± summary table.
